public_rationale: In a post published on 8 July 2024, Zitron forecast that generative AI will not become AGI or science-fiction-style AI. He gave no deadline. The only evidence item is a 27 April 2026 post by Simon Willison (e1). It quotes an October 2025 OpenAI statement that any AGI declaration by OpenAI would be verified by an independent expert panel. The same post argues that the April 2026 partnership terms may have ended the role of that AGI clause. The post does not report any AGI declaration or panel ruling. So the cited evidence does not show a generative-AI system that has been independently verified or broadly accepted as AGI. Under the contract, that is what contradiction requires. The evidence also shows no decisive finding that generative AI cannot reach AGI. Under the contract, that is what support requires. Because there is no deadline, the fact that no AGI has appeared so far cannot confirm the forecast. The claim stays open.
limitations: AGI has no agreed definition, and 'science-fiction' AI has no measurable standard. Any future resolution will depend on which definition is used.

The evidence item covers events only up to 27 April 2026. It does not show whether any AGI declaration, panel review or expert consensus occurred between then and the evaluation date of 28 October 2026.
The evidence does not establish that the expert-panel process described in October 2025 still applies after the April 2026 changes to the partnership.
The packet does not assess informal public statements that AGI has arrived. It notes that these are not verified determinations.

our_interpretation: Read as a forecast with no deadline that generative-AI systems (LLM-based) will never reach human-level general intelligence, nor become sci-fi-style assistants like Jarvis.

Plain reading: the forecast fails if a generative-AI-based system becomes widely accepted (for example, through independent expert verification or broad expert consensus) as general human-level intelligence.
criteria.support_condition: Can only be confirmed for good if the generative-AI paradigm is widely abandoned or shown not to lead to AGI. With no deadline, continued absence of AGI does not settle it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A generative-AI-based system is widely accepted as AGI, for example through verification by the independent expert panel in the Microsoft–OpenAI agreement or broad expert consensus.
